ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen first: I read chat #1 and chat #2 (F9, F10), the driver's post-trip statement (F12) and the rider's complaint — fare and stop only, no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so nothing goes to a person under SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

RD-3 controls. The rider's own message before the segment was driven names a specific place — "Can you stop at Paya Lebar Square? I need to grab a parcel, 3-4 minutes" (F9, 12:21) — the driver accepted ("Ok can", F10, 12:21), and the car did stop there: the only stationary period in the segment is 12:28–12:32 at a point that is neither pickup nor drop-off (F2), matching the requested stop. RD-3(a) therefore exempts the whole way to that named point; the clause fixes the exemption by the naming of the place and a stop there, so neither the duration asked for nor how far the place lay reduces it [F9][F10][F2][RD-3].

RD-5 points the same way. The agreement is a rider message sent at 12:21, before the segment start of 12:25 (F4), and the chat record is complete with every message timestamped (F11), so there is no timing gap to resolve. The authorisation is a specific named place, not a specific named road, and the record places the car AT that named place rather than somewhere else — the stop is at the Paya Lebar Square point the rider named — so the agreement covers this segment; the fact that no road name appears for the driven path does not create an undetermined gap here, because the named object is the destination of this segment and the stop fact ties the segment to it, unlike a bare "go via X" [F9][F10][F11][F2][F4][RD-5].

RD-4 is settled against the driver and needs no exemption from him: no incident was recorded near the route (F15), the speed bands are 4 and 5 (F14, F13), well above the band 1–2 levels, and RD-4(b) does not exempt on its own, and the weather was fair (F16); the driver does not claim traffic, resting on the rider's own stop request [F13][F14][F15][F16][RD-4].

Since the single off-route segment (F4) is exempt, there is no un-exempted kilometre and the RD-2 formula yields zero: 2.97 km × $0.00/km of counted distance, i.e. no refundable distance amount, computed from this trip's rate of $26.72 ÷ 18.95 km = $1.4100/km against the 2.97 km extra of the exempt segment [F4][F5][F8][RD-2]. The billed distance $26.72 (18.95 km), base $3.90, time $7.50, platform $1.47 and $1.15 waiting are all itemised published items for a metered RydeTAXI trip with no surge (F7, F8) [F7][F8][FARE-1]. The waiting fee is the meter's in-trip waiting unit for the 4 min 0 s stop (F6, F2), chargeable under RD-3(c) and not refundable [F6][F2][RD-3]. The rider's complaint that the fare was "much more than the estimate" does not survive the metered structure once the deviation is explained by her own named stop [F1][F3][RD-2].

RD-6 does not apply: the driver has no upheld route dispute in the last 90 days (F18), so the breach is not "repeated" and no account flag is warranted; the rider's clean profile (F17) is not relied on either way [F17][F18][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: The rider named a specific place before the segment: "Can you stop at Paya Lebar Square? I need to grab a parcel, 3-4 minutes" at 12:21 (F9), accepted by the driver (F10). The car stopped there — the 12:28–12:32 stationary period at a non-pickup/non-drop-off point (F2) is inside the segment, and the message is a rider message sent before the 12:25 segment start. RD-3(a) exempts the whole way to the named point regardless of stop length or distance, and RD-5 confirms consent given before the segment whose scope covers the route serving that named stop [F4][F9][F10][F2][RD-3][RD-5].

rejected_claims.reason: The trace's RD-1 screen does show one off-route segment (F4), but RD-1's own terms subject every segment to RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 review, and this segment is excused as the rider-named stop under RD-3(a) [F4][F9][F10][F2][RD-1][RD-3].

Reading the rider's message as exempting only a route to the point plus exactly 4 minutes is not what RD-3(a) says: naming the place exempts the way there and the stop, and the duration asked for or the distance to the place cannot reduce it [F9][F2][F4][RD-3][RD-5].

The deviation is excused not by the driver's post-trip statement (F12), which is only a claim, but by the rider's own timestamped message (F9, F10) — so the G11 point about verbal agreement does not bite, and the gap to Paya Lebar Square is the way to the rider-named stop [F9][F10][F12][F4][RD-3][RD-5].

The fare facts (F8, F5) themselves cannot create a refund: RD-2 refunds only kilometres on an un-exempted segment, and the segment these excess kilometres belong to is exempt, so the billed excess stays [F5][F8][F4][RD-2].

The claimed $4.19 (2.97 km × $1.4100/km) assumes 2.97 un-exempted kilometres, but the only segment carrying them is exempt under RD-3(a), so the sum of un-exempted extra_km is zero and no amount is payable [F4][F5][RD-2][RD-3].

The driver's point that the $4.91 residual is consumed by the rider's stop is correct in outcome but incomplete as stated; the exemption comes from RD-3(a)/RD-5 on the whole segment, not merely from the residual being small, and RD-6 is not engaged because F18 shows no prior upheld dispute [F5][F4][F18][RD-3][RD-6].
